Messages.Author: Jack Ryan
Messages.Body:
Here I am bringing up this card again. But after coming from a
storyline tournament, and sitting at a table where this card let two
players become one to split the table.

My question is: Why is this card not banned in tournament play?

The only comments I hear are about how two players, who know each
other, use it to team up and decide how they want to split the table.

I come from a small town, and it hard to get players to play. Now one
person will not play again because he was on the receiving end of the
Succubus Club.

I just want to start right this instant a campaign to ban this card
from tournaments. My vote is to ban it. Playing in tournaments is
fun, and when I get some people together and go out-of-town to play
with other groups, I don't want to travel home with them after
watching Succubus Club do its dirty work to them.

Lets get together and ban it NOW.

> must always play for a game win, unless that's basically impossible.

This isn't just a matter of not going for the win, this is a charge of
straightforward collusion. Someone put SC in their deck with the idea to
team up with friends before the tournament started. It's collusion if it's
true, though the problem is proving that's why the SC is in there.

> This occurs with or without Succubus Club, and judges have to enforce
> this (and collusion) with or without Succubus Club.

Yes, but SC makes it *vastly* harder for others at the table to do anything
if the judge can't find enough evidence to disallow the trades. SC can
also make the judge's call less clear.

SC is a ridiculous kingmaker too. More so than any other reason to ban it,
it is that property that should get it out of the tournament circle. If
you don't have Sudden Reversal or an anti-location card in your hand when
it's played, the game can instantly fall apart as one Meth decides to give
his 5 small caps and all his pool to another player, who now utterly
annhilates his prey with his ill gotten gains. And people will defend SC
saying "well you just have to hit the guy who received everything cross
table" -- look you have maybe 2 turns before the receiver mows down his
prey, so you need to have those bum's rushes or whatever in your hand every
time SC hits the table... and if the receiver gets to take his turn before
you? GG. You can't even hope to cycle into the cross table weapons you're
packing because if you take forward/backward actions you're just weakening
their ability to hit the receiver, and you're going to need more than 1
person hitting that player.
Allowing players to take a dive, by transfering out, or taking a bunch of
clearly suicidal actions, is fine. I've seen people get spited, I've been
spited, etc. etc.. It's annoying, but in no way is it overpowering. With
SC, a player taking a dive is vastly more likely to take the rest of the
table for said swim. How does a card that lets a player in a weak position
decide the winner make for good tournament games? Sure, they won't always
be able to pick the winner, but I'm willing to bet that someone using SC
could play kingmaker with at least 60%... change that to 80% or higher if
they actually tune their deck around SC's kingmaker properties.

I was involved in this game, in fact I was the one who sat between the
two doing the trading via SC. My predator made a deal with my prey to
split the table (3-2 in favor of my predator). Also for
clarification, it was the 3rd round of preliminaries, so anyone
leaving after the game who wasn't a finalist was moot.

Without my predator's help of a pool donation to my prey would have
been ousted. I didn't see the split as illegal, as my prey wouldn't
have gotten any VPs had he not struck the deal. The deal seemed to be
perfectly legal and honest. I've played with one of the guys involved
in the deal several times, and I think he was honestly just exploiting
a legal but cheesy card to achieve a game win.

I don't like the way the card functions mechanically. It is
completely unlike any other card in the game in that it facilitates
the free sharing of resources to enable table split deals, which I
think is cheesy in the extreme. It makes it too easy for two people
to decide the outcome of the game.

The card enables collusion, and just because there is no evidence of
collusion doesn't mean that there isn't any. Remember that collusion
is by definition secret and therefore extremely hard to prove in a
case such as a tournament like this. (keeping in mind that the
presence of the card does not mean that there _is_ collusion, only
that it enables collusion)
